study: Droop et al. 2016 (Strategic Reading Instruction [SRI] teacher training; Grades 3-4 reading comprehension)
eval_evidence: Program developed and evaluated by the study authors: the second author 'wrote the manual for the teachers' and supervised the coaches; the authors designed and ran the SRI program and the trial. (An independent Radboud researcher administered some tests, but the evaluation itself is by the program developers.)
developer_evidence: Teacher training was given by the project; coaching 'was performed by three certified and experienced coaches under supervision of the second author' (the program developer who wrote the manual).
cascade_evidence: Teachers were trained and coached by certified coaches operating directly under the supervision of the developer-author; treated as developer-direct delivery rather than an independent train-the-trainer cascade.
counterfactual_evidence: Control group used the regular school reading curriculum (business-as-usual); experimental schools were restricted from their own comprehension curriculum to prevent diffusion, but the control simply continued normal practice.
coaching_evidence: PD = two 3-hour training meetings (in September) per grade-year, plus a single classroom observation in November each year, each observation followed by one coaching/feedback session. Light/periodic, not recurring in-class coaching cycles.
student_dose_evidence: Intervention changes the teacher's reading-comprehension instruction (strategy instruction during regular read-aloud/reading lessons); no tutoring, pull-out, or extra student dose.
maturity_evidence: Two-year program implemented across Grade 3 (Year 1) and Grade 4 (Year 2); the significant primary intervention effects were at the end of Grade 4 (the Year-2 wave), after a prior implementation year (Grade-3/Year-1 effects were null/interim).
